<section class="guide-overview container-xs xs-mb6 md-mt6">
<h2 class="xs-mb3">Calgary City Guide</h2>

<div class="xs-mb5 sm-py3 xs-flex xs-flex-wrap">
<div class="xs-col-6 sm-col-4 sm-border-right-lighter xs-p3 sm-py0 xs-text-center">
<div class="xs-mb1 xs-text-1 text-blue bold">1.1M</div>
<div class="text-secondary xs-text-5">Population</div>
</div>
<div class="xs-col-6 sm-col-4 sm-border-right-lighter xs-p3 sm-py0 xs-text-center">
<div class="xs-mb1 xs-text-1 text-blue bold">10.9%</div>
<div class="text-secondary xs-text-5">Population Growth</div>
</div>
<div class="xs-col-12 sm-col-4 xs-p3 sm-py0 xs-text-center">
<div class="xs-mb1 xs-text-1 text-blue bold">6%</div>
<div class="text-secondary xs-text-5">Unemployment</div>
</div>
</div>

<p>Calgary is a vibrant and diverse city, and while it is known for the Calgary Stampede,&nbsp;it has so much to offer! The city is home to more than 1.3 million residents, making it Alberta&#39;s largest city and the 4th-largest in Canada. Additionally, Calgary has been booming over the last several years and in 2023, Calgary boasted the highest population growth among major cities in Canada, with 6% growth compared to 2022. Calgary led the country in net interprovincial migration in 2023 as many Canadians from other provinces made their way to Stampede City. Over the years, it&#39#39;s also become an economic powerhouse, offering excellent job opportunities for trade workers and C-suite executives alike.</p><p>Situated on the Bow River in Southern Alberta, the area now known as multiple Indigenous groups have inhabited Calgary for thousands of years. The first European settlers built Fort Calgary in 1875 as a post for the North-West Mounted Police. Later, the federal government began to offer leases for cattle ranches, leading to an influx of residents.</p><p>Now, the city is recognized as a leader in the Canadian oil and gas industries and a forerunner in the region&#39;s economic expansion. Personal and family incomes are relatively high, although, recently, unemployment has been on the rise. Still, the city doesn&#39;t rely solely on oil and gas. It&#39;s known as one of Canada&#39;s global financial centres, and small businesses and self-employment levels rank among the highest in Canada. By diversifying away from the oil and gas sector, Calgary&#39;s labour force in other areas has grown. As of 2021, healthcare and social assistance accounted for 13% of the workforce. Additionally, professional, scientific and technical services accounted for 12% of the workforce. Compared to 5% who worked in mining and oil and gas extraction.</p><p>The top three companies by number of employees in Calgary are Suncor Energy, Canadian Pacific Railway and Enbridge. However, Calgary has the 4th-highest concentration of head offices in Canada, behind Toronto, Montreal and Vancouver.</p><p>While household income in Calgary is higher than the national average, and housing is affordable, what really makes this city great is its proximity to the wilderness. Sitting in Southern Alberta, Calgary is a short drive from the Canadian Rocky Mountains and resort towns like Banff and Canmore. This proximity to nature means city residents can have an exceptional work/life balance ideal for just about everyone, particularly the outdoor enthusiast.</p><p>Located in Mountain Time (GMT -6), the average temperature in Calgary varies widely throughout the year. In the summer, the average high temperature throughout the day lands around 20 to 24 degrees Celsius, while in winter, the coldest winter nights can drop as low as -30 degrees Celsius. However, Calgary is one of the sunniest cities in Canada, boasting an average of 333 days of sunshine per year, so you can enjoy the amazing nature and outdoor activities year-round.</p><p>You may be wondering if it is expensive to live in Calgary. According to the <a href="https://www.livingwagealberta.ca/reports">Alberta Living Wage Network</a>, the living wage in Calgary is $23.70. This living wage is lower than other major cities in Canada. For example, the living wage in Toronto and Vancouver are $25.05 and $25.68, respectively. In addition, property taxes are relatively low at 0.64861%.</p><p>All things considered, Calgary is an excellent option for Canadians looking to put down roots in a city with good job opportunities, affordable housing, and a livable lifestyle. It is considered the fifth most livable city in the world by the <a href="https://www.calgaryeconomicdevelopment.com/newsroom/calgary-rises-in-ranks-to-fifth-most-livable-city-in-the-world-in-2024">Economist Intelligence Unit</a>. The city offers a wide range of housing options for those looking to buy a home in Calgary. You can find budget-friendly <a href="https://www.zolo.ca/calgary-real-estate/condos">condos</a>, newly built <a href="https://www.zolo.ca/calgary-real-estate/townhouses">townhouses</a> and plenty of <a href="https://www.zolo.ca/calgary-real-estate/houses">detached homes</a> with yard space.</p> </section>

<p>At this point in time, Calgary&#039;s median sale price is $551,000. This number is determined by finding the mid-point price of all property sold within a specified period of time. For example, if 279 condos sold last month and only 602 detached homes sold in the same time frame, then the median price would reflect the mid-point between the 279 condos and the 602 detached homes sold during that time. At present, Calgary has 1,737 houses for sale, 1,153 townhomes for sale and 1,375 condos for sale.</p>
<p>For more information on the current state of Calgary&#39;s real estate market, check out the <a href="https://www.zolo.ca/calgary-real-estate/trends">Market Stats</a>.</p><p>Still, for the best strategies, talk to a local Calgary real estate agent who knows the city and can guide you to the best neighbourhood to meet your needs and budget.</p><p>To see the latest <a href="https://www.zolo.ca/calgary-real-estate/houses">detached homes</a>, <a href="https://www.zolo.ca/calgary-real-estate/condos">condos</a>, or <a href="https://www.zolo.ca/calgary-real-estate/townhouses">townhouses</a> for sale in Calgary, check out the city&#39;s MLS &reg; board listings.</p> </section>
<section class="guide-neighbourhoods container-xs xs-mb6">
<h2 class="xs-mb3">Neighbourhoods</h2>
<p>The city of Calgary was first established using a grid system. Centre Street and the Bow River offer the geographical axis that splits the city into four quadrants. This pragmatic city structure could leave you with the impression that the city is one monolithic housing market. It&#39;s not. There are distinct communities. These communities offer colour and depth to what is now a vibrant and youthful city. This diversity is good news for buyers looking for a variety of homes for sale in this large western Canadian city.</p><p>Take, for instance, the communities of <a href="https://www.zolo.ca/calgary-real-estate/beltline">Beltline</a> and <a href="https://www.zolo.ca/calgary-real-estate/mission">Mission</a>, which are located just south of the downtown core. There&#39;s a great selection of new and older rentals and <a href="https://www.zolo.ca/calgary-real-estate/condos">Calgary condos</a>. But the biggest attraction is walkability. Beltline residents are minutes from the city&#39;s rapid transit light rail train, which runs through downtown. Both communities are a short walk from the popular 17th Avenue SW. This street is the commercial strip famously dubbed the Red Mile after waves of Calgary Flames fans took to the streets to cheer on their hockey team. Calgary&#39;s oldest neighbourhood, <a href="https://www.zolo.ca/calgary-real-estate/inglewood">Inglewood</a>, is an excellent choice for art and music lovers. You can find older family homes in <a href="https://www.zolo.ca/calgary-real-estate/bowness">Bowness</a> and <a href="https://www.zolo.ca/calgary-real-estate/varsity">Varsity</a>, which are ideal neighbourhoods if you want proximity to the University of Calgary.</p><p>Condos are growing in popularity in Calgary, and condo sales make up close to one-third of all homes sold in the Calgary real estate market. If you&#39;re searching for a condo to call home, check out the neighbourhoods of <a href="https://www.zolo.ca/calgary-real-estate/beltline">Beltine</a>, <a href="https://www.zolo.ca/calgary-real-estate/university-district">University District</a>, and <a href="https://www.zolo.ca/calgary-real-estate/hillhurst">Hillhurst</a>. Here, you can find semi-detached houses, row houses, and condos, plus new developments that are currently under construction.</p><p>If you want to live close to work in downtown Calgary, there are several mixed-use neighbourhoods, including <a href="https://www.zolo.ca/calgary-real-estate/chinatown">Chinatown</a>, <a href="https://www.zolo.ca/calgary-real-estate/downtown-east-village">East Village</a>, and the <a href="https://www.zolo.ca/calgary-real-estate/downtown-west-end">West End</a>. These high-density neighbourhoods offer parks, historic buildings, shopping and housing options like condos and apartment buildings.</p><p>Recent city-wide rezoning has been approved to help build more housing options in this growing city. These changes will allow for higher-density housing, such as apartments, condos, and row houses, to be built in neighbourhoods previously established as single-family zones.</p><p>You may be wondering where to find the most expensive neighbourhoods in Calgary. You can find higher-end homes in <a href="https://www.zolo.ca/calgary-real-estate/altadore">Altadore</a>, <a href="https://www.zolo.ca/calgary-real-estate/bel-aire">Bel Aire</a>, and <a href="https://www.zolo.ca/calgary-real-estate/aspen-woods">Aspen Woods</a>, where the asking prices are typically over $1 million. On the other hand, the most affordable neighbourhoods in Calgary are <a href="https://www.zolo.ca/calgary-real-estate/red-carpet">Red Carpet</a>, <a href="https://www.zolo.ca/calgary-real-estate/windsor-park">Windsor Park</a> and <a href="https://www.zolo.ca/calgary-real-estate/manchester">Manchester</a>.</p><p>To help start your property search, check out our neighbourhood rankings. Using the latest data, all communities are ranked based on how quickly houses sell, the sale price and how many listings are currently available. Of course, loving where you live is important, so use the rankings to narrow down your choices before spending some quality time soaking up the local vibe and walking through a few <a href="https://www.zolo.ca/calgary-real-estate/open-houses">Calgary open houses</a>.</p>

<section class="guide-cities container-xs xs-mb6">
<h2 class="xs-mb3">Nearby Cities</h2>
<p>Many buyers opt to purchase in a nearby city and commute to work. These buyers want larger homes and lots with good commuter access to <a href="https://www.zolo.ca/calgary-real-estate/downtown">Calgary&#39;s downtown core</a>. Good options include <a href="https://www.zolo.ca/calgary-real-estate/bowness">Bowness</a>, <a href="https://www.zolo.ca/calgary-real-estate/brentwood">Brentwood</a> and <a href="https://www.zolo.ca/calgary-real-estate/huntington-hills">Huntington Hills</a>, which are within a 20-minute drive or less of downtown Calgary. These neighbourhoods are technically part of Calgary, but they offer established communities of single-family detached homes and convenient access to amenities.</p><p>For those looking for an easy commute to downtown, look for neighbourhoods closer to the highway or commuter train stations, such as <a href="https://www.zolo.ca/calgary-real-estate/shawnessy">Shawnessy</a> or <a href="https://www.zolo.ca/calgary-real-estate/royal-oak">Royal Oak</a>. These communities boast a higher-than-average median household income and easy access to grocery stores, cafes and restaurants.</p><p>Even cities that require a bit longer commute, such as <a href="https://www.zolo.ca/chestermere-real-estate">Chestermere</a>, <a href="https://www.zolo.ca/airdrie-real-estate">Airdrie</a>, and <a href="https://www.zolo.ca/cochrane-real-estate">Cochrane</a>, are options as they offer more affordable detached homes on larger lots within a 35-minute drive of downtown Calgary.</p>

<section class="guide-demographics container-xs xs-mb6">
<h2 class="xs-mb3">Demographics</h2>
<p>More people are moving to Calgary than ever before. In 2022 and 2023, Calgary led the country in interprovincial migration, as many Ontarians and British Columbians left the high home prices of Toronto and Vancouver behind to find affordable housing. However, permanent immigration and temporary international residents are also a driving force behind Calgary&#39;s recent growth, accounting for 27% and 36% of the population, respectively.</p><p>Buying a house means becoming part of a community. Before you buy, get to know your neighbours. For a quick snapshot consider these Calgary demographics, such as median age, schools and income. All information is collected from <a href="https://www12.statcan.gc.ca/census-recensement/2021/dp-pd/prof/details/page.cfm?Lang=E&amp;GENDERlist=1,2,3&amp;STATISTIClist=1,4&amp;HEADERlist=0&amp;DGUIDlist=2021A00054806016&amp;SearchText=calgary">Statistics Canada</a> census data.</p>

<section class="guide-schools container-xs xs-mb6">
<h2 class="xs-mb3">Schools</h2>
<p>Families interested in setting down roots may want to consider Calgary&#39;s top-rated elementary and secondary schools. The top five schools in each category are below to help you narrow down your <a href="https://www.zolo.ca/calgary-real-estate/trends">Calgary housing market</a> search.</p><p>Calgary residents have plenty of options for post-secondary education, including universities and private and community colleges.&nbsp;</p><p>The <a href="https://www.ucalgary.ca/">University of Calgary</a> offers over 250 undergraduate programs and numerous graduate programs over several campuses across the city. Mount Royal University, located in the <a href="https://www.zolo.ca/calgary-real-estate/lincoln-park">Lincoln Park</a> neighbourhood, offers various degrees, diplomas, and certificate programs.</p><p>Calgary&#39;s only community college, Bow Valley College, is located in downtown Calgary and offers education opportunities in business, entertainment arts, community studies, health and wellness, and technology.</p><p>Lastly, several private career colleges across the city offer programs in art and design, business, healthcare, esthetics, massage therapy, pilot training, marketing, legal, paramedicine, and many more faculties.</p>

<section class="guide-commuters container-xs xs-mb6">
<h2 class="xs-mb3">Commuters</h2>
<p>Calgary is a large city. If you rely on the city&#39;s public transit system, rapid transit options include the C-Train, a light rail passenger train and several bus routes. With the planned expansions, getting to the Calgary International Airport, South Health Campus Hospital and Aurora Business Park will get even easier. In the long term, the city hopes to add high-speed rail service to other municipalities such as Banff, Canmore, and Edmonton.</p><p>If you&#39;d rather bike, check out neighbourhoods close to the Bow River, like <a href="https://www.zolo.ca/calgary-real-estate/sunalta">Sunalta</a>, where there is easy access to bike trails like Bowness Park and the Bow River Bike Trail. Calgary has North America&#39;s most extensive bikeway network, with approximately 1,000 kilometres of regional pathways. In addition, the government has recently invested in protecting and extending bike lanes in Calgary.</p><p>Many communities in Calgary, including <a href="https://www.zolo.ca/calgary-real-estate/beltline">Beltline</a> and <a href="https://www.zolo.ca/calgary-real-estate/cliff-bungalow">Cliff Bungalow</a>, are considered walkable. However, many Calgarians opt to drive, and several major roadways connect downtown. The average commuting time for those driving to work is 23 minutes, shorter than other major cities in Canada, including Toronto, Montreal, and Vancouver.</p><p>YYC Calgary International Airport is one of the busiest airports in Canada and the home base of Canadian airline WestJet. You can book nonstop flights from Calgary to many destinations in Canada, Europe, Mexico, Asia, and the USA. Calgary Transit connects the airport with the downtown core.</p><p>To better understand how city residents commute, consider the data collected by <a href="https://www12.statcan.gc.ca/census-recensement/2021/dp-pd/prof/details/page.cfm?Lang=E&amp;GENDERlist=1,2,3&amp;STATISTIClist=1,4&amp;HEADERlist=0&amp;DGUIDlist=2021A00054806016&amp;SearchText=calgary">Statistics Canada.</a></p> <div class="sm-pt3 xs-flex xs-flex-wrap">

<section class="guide-localscoop container-xs">
<h2 class="xs-mb3">Local Scoop</h2>
<p>For locals, Calgary is a great place to live, work and play, especially for outdoor enthusiasts. You&#39;ll find numerous parks in the city, including Prince&#39;s Island Park, Fish Creek Provincial Park, Bowness Park, and Nose Hill Park, where you can walk and hike in the warm months and cross-country ski or skate in the colder months.</p><p>Within a two-hour drive, you can explore national parks and National Historic Sites with plenty of hiking and camping opportunities, perfect for weekend getaways outside the big city.</p><p><a href="https://www.zolo.ca/calgary-real-estate/downtown">Downtown Calgary</a> is a hub for theatre, galleries and museums. With top-rated restaurants and icons like the Calgary Tower, there is always plenty to do. We recommend spending a sunny afternoon on the patio of the iconic 17th Avenue pub, The Ship.</p><p>For foodies, Calgary has plenty of restaurant options, ranging from fine dining at <a href="https://rougecalgary.com/">Rouge</a> to the legendary Tubby Dog, now known as <a href="https://tubbybar.com/">Tubby&#39;s Bar</a>. Of course, many restaurants will serve Alberta Beef as the star of the show, but you can find a wide variety of cuisines.</p><p>For sports lovers, Calgary is home to several professional teams, including the Calgary Flames NHL team, the Calgary Stampeders CFL team, and the Calgary Roughnecks NLL team. Additionally, you can check out the Olympic Plaza. Built for the 1988 Winter Olympics, it&#39;s now a multi-purpose space offering outdoor skating, inline skating, special events, and more.</p><p>In July, almost the entire city will don cowboy boots and Stetsons to celebrate the <a href="https://www.calgarystampede.com/">Calgary Stampede</a>. The event, which has roots that go back to 1886, draws the whole city out to celebrate this long, rich rodeo history. There are community pancake breakfasts, beer festivals, and events for young and old throughout the city.</p><p>In addition to the Stampede, there are other festivals throughout the year, including the Calgary Folk Music Festival, the Annual Heritage Day Festival, Calgary Pride and the Calgary International Film Festival.</p><p>Families will be interested in the National Music Centre. This interactive exhibit lets kids try out a variety of instruments, including the electric guitar, drums and a voice recording room. For a more historical experience, consider a day at the Heritage Park Historical Village. Costumed actors roam the village, recreating life in the city in the early 20th century. A day of pure amusement can be found at Calaway Park, Western Canada&#39;s largest outdoor family amusement park. <a href="https://www.calgaryzoo.com/">The Wilder Institute Calgary Zoo</a> is a popular spot for all ages to learn about wildlife conservation.</p> </section>
